findings.evidence: trigger pull_request_target + checkout of PR head at step 'actions/checkout@v4'
findings.message: Job 'triage' runs on pull_request_target (secrets and a privileged token available) and checks out PR-head code — attacker-controlled code executes in a privileged context (pwn-request pattern).
findings.remediation: Split the workflow: handle untrusted PR code under the unprivileged pull_request event, and keep pull_request_target jobs from checking out PR-head refs. If PR code must be processed, do it without secrets and with permissions: read-all or less.

findings.message: Untrusted context 'github.event.pull_request.title' is interpolated directly into a run script in job 'triage'. Its value is expanded before the shell parses the line, so crafted input becomes part of the command.
findings.remediation: Route the value through env: and reference it as a quoted shell variable, e.g. env: TITLE: ${{ <expr> }} then run: echo "$TITLE". The shell then receives the value as data, never as command text.

findings.message: Third-party action 'example-org/super-linter' is pinned to a mutable reference (@v3). A compromised or retagged release changes what this pipeline executes.
findings.remediation: Pin to a full commit SHA (uses: owner/action@<40-hex-sha> with a version comment) and update via a dependency bot; tags and branches are mutable.

findings.message: Secret(s) FIXTURE_FAKE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN are written to the job log by an echo/print in job 'triage'. Log masking is best-effort and fails on transformed values.
findings.remediation: Never print secret expressions; pass secrets via env: to the consuming process and rely on masked, non-printed usage.
findings.step_name: notify (echoes a secret reference; name is obviously fake)

findings.evidence: secrets.* referenced in an untrusted-reachable job
findings.message: Job 'triage' uses repository secrets while reachable from an untrusted trigger (workflow triggered by pull_request_target). Combined with attacker-influenced execution this is the secret-exfiltration setup.
findings.remediation: Move secret-using work to a workflow that runs only on trusted events, or gate it behind environment protection rules with required review.
findings.step_name: notify (echoes a secret reference; name is obviously fake)

findings.message: Step 'install tool (unverified remote install; inert example domain)' pipes a remote download directly into an interpreter — the pipeline executes whatever the remote host serves, unverified.
findings.remediation: Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum (sha256sum -c) or signature, then execute; or install from a pinned package.
findings.step_name: install tool (unverified remote install; inert example domain)

findings.message: Untrusted context 'github.event.head_commit' is interpolated directly into a run script in job 'build'. Its value is expanded before the shell parses the line, so crafted input becomes part of the command.
findings.remediation: Route the value through env: and reference it as a quoted shell variable, e.g. env: TITLE: ${{ <expr> }} then run: echo "$TITLE". The shell then receives the value as data, never as command text.
findings.step_name: print commit message (injection sink; inert payload)

findings.message: permissions: write-all on workflow grants the token every scope (contents, packages, actions, id-token…) — far more than any single job needs.
findings.remediation: Add an explicit least-privilege block, e.g. permissions: { contents: read } at the workflow top level, widening only the scopes a specific job needs.

findings.message: First-party action 'actions/setup-python' is pinned to a mutable reference (@v5). A compromised or retagged release changes what this pipeline executes.
findings.remediation: Pin to a full commit SHA (uses: owner/action@<40-hex-sha> with a version comment) and update via a dependency bot; tags and branches are mutable.

findings.message: First-party action 'actions/checkout' is pinned to a mutable reference (@v4). A compromised or retagged release changes what this pipeline executes.
findings.remediation: Pin to a full commit SHA (uses: owner/action@<40-hex-sha> with a version comment) and update via a dependency bot; tags and branches are mutable.

findings.message: actions/checkout in job 'triage' persists the repository token into .git config (the default) in a workflow reachable from PR-driven events — later steps and checked-out tooling can read it from disk.
findings.remediation: Add 'persist-credentials: false' to the checkout step unless a later step genuinely needs the persisted token.
